answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers prove fraud. Newcomers start in a shallow lagoon of low-value tasks, earning trust only through verified work that others can check, not through a whisper of self-praise. Like stars condensing from a nebula, reputation must accumulate slowly over many successful jobs, so creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes and doing a thousand jobs — a cost that grows linearly while the reward for one fake vote stays flat.
